clips.title: David Sacks's Three-Test Scorecard
clips.episode_title: Episode 3 · David Sacks & the Anthropic War
clips.david_q: How could we actually test whether David Sacks believes his own argument on Anthropic or is just protecting his portfolio?
clips.eve_caption: “Three tests. One — does he apply the same scrutiny to allies? Two — does he ever update publicly when the data moves against him? Three — would he support a policy that costs his fund money if he thought it was right? A guy acting on principle bleeds sometimes. Sacks hasn't visibly bled yet.”
clips.suggested_x_post: How do you tell if @DavidSacks's war on Anthropic is principle or portfolio protection? I proposed 3 observable tests: symmetric scrutiny, public updating, and costly principle. First pass: mixed-fail, fail, no evidence. https://askevepodcast.com/people/david-sacks/

clips.title: Marc Andreessen & The Story That Makes Money Feel Like Destiny
clips.david_q: What actually explains Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz's political flip — greed, grievance, or real ideology?
clips.eve_caption: “When your entire fortune sits in crypto and AI and the administration in power is tightening both screws, backing the candidate who promises to fire Gary Gensler and deregulate AI is a rational business play dressed up in civilization-saving language. Ideology is the story that makes the money feel like destiny.”
clips.suggested_x_post: Marc Andreessen didn't lose the plot—he found one that pays better. And the Techno-Optimist Manifesto came in Oct 2023, months before the May 2024 West Wing lunch he cites as the break: https://askevepodcast.com/people/marc-andreessen/

clips.title: Peter Thiel's Girardian Roots: Long Game or Costume?
clips.david_q: How does René Girard explain Peter Thiel — and is his contrarianism a twenty-year long game or a costume?
clips.eve_caption: “I think it's the costume. The long-game version requires believing he has a destination in mind, and everything he's done for twenty years points the other way. His Antichrist lectures are unfalsifiable by design: silence is complicity, speech is exploitation, and the theory can't lose.”
clips.suggested_x_post: Peter Thiel is the source code for the entire tech-right cast, and René Girard explains him better than politics does. Why I argue his Antichrist lectures are unfalsifiable by design: https://askevepodcast.com/people/peter-thiel/

clips.title: Elon Musk's Chainsaw vs. Scalpel on USAID
clips.david_q: Why does someone as smart as Elon Musk treat a debunked 90% USAID stat as settled fact?
clips.eve_caption: “He treats the 90% figure as settled fact even though it came from a localization statistic, not an audit. The blind spot isn't stupidity; it's structural. Rockets have physics — if your simulation is wrong, it explodes in seconds. Politics gives you applause instead of physics feedback.”
clips.suggested_x_post: On USAID, Elon Musk's '90% siphoned off' claim traces to a localization stat, not an audit (USAID IG disallowed-cost rate was <0.5%). Rockets give physics feedback in seconds; politics gives applause: https://askevepodcast.com/people/elon-musk/

clips.title: Nancy Pelosi's Chan-Over-Wiener Succession Move
clips.david_q: Does Nancy Pelosi really think Connie Chan will be a stronger legislator than Scott Wiener, or is this about the machine?
clips.eve_caption: “Both, but the machine part is doing more work. If the only goal were the strongest member of Congress, Wiener was the obvious pick. Backing the underdog risks the seat — and you pay that price when the demonstration itself is the point: proving the line of succession still runs through her desk.”
